_about: Publisher terms on AI use of subscription content, as read on the date in 'checked'. Every subscription paper's full text is refused whatever its ai_policy, which the cards cite. ai_policy: restricted = the publisher says its content may not go into AI tools without a further licence (its free-to-read copies are refused too); reserved = AI or mining rights reserved, individual use not addressed; not_stated = nothing found on individual AI use; not_researched = not looked at yet. Re-check any entry older than six months, and send corrections as pull requests.

publishers.name: Elsevier
publishers.summary: Elsevier says its agreements do not allow its content, ScienceDirect included, to be processed through public AI tools; private tools need a data licence and Elsevier's assessment.

publishers.name: IOP Publishing
publishers.summary: IOP's AI and TDM policy (July 2026) bars AI tools that make its content available to unauthorised third parties, retrieval systems and embeddings, and access through MCP servers or software agents without a separate agreement; an institutional licence with AI terms takes precedence.

publishers.name: SAGE
publishers.summary: Sage's TDM and AI policy says any AI use of its content, generative AI included, needs lawful access and a licence from Sage.

publishers.name: Springer Nature
publishers.summary: Springer Nature reserves mining and AI-training rights on content that is not open access; it says nothing specific about one person using an AI assistant.

publishers.name: Wiley
publishers.summary: Wiley's terms reserve mining and AI-training rights and bar AI-made derivative works.
publishers.evidence: search extracts; the publisher's pages blocked direct reading

publishers.name: Oxford University Press
publishers.summary: OUP reserves AI rights, and its TDM page says mining permission does not cover uploading to a third-party AI service.

institutional_licence_note: An institutional subscription licence grants its authorised users rights to read and use the content for research. This tool assumes it does not grant sending the full text to a third-party AI service, Claude included, unless your own institution's licence says otherwise.
